title: Smallest Number in Infinite Set
statement:
Build a class `SmallestInfiniteSet` that models a set which starts out holding every positive integer: 1, 2, 3 and so on without end.

- `SmallestInfiniteSet()` creates the set with all positive integers in it.
- `popSmallest()` takes the smallest number currently in the set out of it and returns that number.
- `addBack(num)` puts the positive integer `num` into the set again. If `num` is already present, the call changes nothing.
constraints: At most 1000 calls in total are made to popSmallest and addBack
notes:
## Intuition

Only finitely many numbers are ever missing from the set, so describe it by what changed. Every number from `next` upward has never been popped and is still present. Below `next`, a number is present only if it was popped and then added back. Those returned numbers live in a min-heap, and the smallest of them (if any) is always smaller than `next`. A brute force could keep the set of removed numbers and scan upward from 1 on every pop, which costs O(answer) per call.

## Approach

1. Start with `next = 1`, an empty `heap` and an empty `inHeap` set.
2. `popSmallest`: if `heap` is empty, return `next` and advance it. Otherwise remove the heap's minimum (move the last item to the root and sift it down), drop it from `inHeap`, and return it.
3. `addBack(num)`: if `num >= next` it is already present; if `inHeap` has it, it is also present. In both cases do nothing.
4. Otherwise record `num` in `inHeap`, push it onto `heap` and sift it up.

## Example 1, step by step

`addBack(2)` does nothing because `2 >= next = 1`. Three pops find the heap empty and return 1, 2 and 3, leaving `next = 4`. `addBack(1)` sees `1 < 4`, so 1 goes into the heap. The next pop takes 1 from the heap; the heap is then empty, so the last two pops return 4 and 5. Output: `[null, null, 1, 2, 3, null, 1, 4, 5]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(log k) per call, where k is the heap size (at most the number of `addBack` calls).
- Space: O(k) for `heap` and `inHeap`.

## Pitfalls

- Adding a number twice must not create two heap entries; `inHeap` guards against that.
- A number at or above `next` was never removed, so pushing it would make it pop twice.
- Delete the popped value from `inHeap`, or a later `addBack` of it is wrongly ignored.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `next` | smallest number never popped; all numbers from here up are present |
| `heap` | min-heap of numbers below `next` that were added back |
| `inHeap` | the same numbers as a set, for O(1) duplicate checks |
| `smallest` | in `popSmallest`, the popped minimum; in `siftDown`, the position of the smallest of the item and its children |
| `last` | the heap's last item, moved to the root after a pop |
| `index`, `parent`, `left`, `right` | positions used while sifting the heap |
